title: Duplicate orders

headlines.label: Scenarios that end with more than one PayPal order (100 duplicate-prone scenarios, current payment policy)
headlines.baseline: random request id per attempt: 0 of 100
headlines.note: Simulation of PayPal's documented PayPal-Request-Id idempotency; no PayPal call is made. 100 orders for 100 intended purchases. Before the fix for lost PayPal answers: 10 of 100 (random id: 20 of 100).

headlines.label: Same 100 scenarios before the fix (lost PayPal answer released the hold and the buyer heard "nothing was charged")
headlines.baseline: random request id per attempt: 20 of 100
headlines.note: Before fix, kept for comparison. 110 orders for 100 intended purchases.

headlines.label: Repeats of one confirmation (double-click, triple confirm, resend after timeout, re-say, two tabs) that end in a second order
headlines.baseline: random request id per attempt: 0 of 90
headlines.note: Simulation of PayPal's documented PayPal-Request-Id idempotency; no PayPal call is made. Before the fix: 0 of 90 (random id: 10 of 90).

headlines.label: Resend after a lost PayPal response, same confirmation: second order created
headlines.baseline: random request id per attempt: 0 of 10
headlines.note: Before the fix: 0 of 10 with the bound id, 10 of 10 with a random id, so the bound id alone stopped it. Now the resend is refused before any new PayPal call.

headlines.label: Lost PayPal response, buyer buys again on a new readback within minutes: second order created
headlines.baseline: random request id per attempt: 0 of 10
headlines.note: Before the fix: 10 of 10 (random id: 10 of 10). Now refused while the earlier order's outcome is unknown.

headlines.label: Lost PayPal response, buyer buys the same item again after the 10-minute duplicate window: second order created
headlines.baseline: random request id per attempt: 0 of 10
headlines.note: Separate probe, not in the 100. Now refused (OUTCOME_UNKNOWN) while the earlier order is unsettled, with no time limit. Before this fix (hold kept, 10-minute look-back only): 10 of 10.

headlines.label: Same probe before the unknown-outcome block (hold kept, duplicate check looks back 10 minutes only)
headlines.baseline: random request id per attempt: 10 of 10
headlines.note: Before fix, kept for comparison: a snapshot older than 12 minutes is re-taken (new cart hash) and the look-back had ended.

headlines.label: Buyer comes back after a lost PayPal response, then would buy again: second order created
headlines.note: Reconciliation re-sent the original request id; PayPal returned the original order and it was settled once in 10 of 10. The simulated buyer, told it went through, does not buy again.

limitations: Simulation of PayPal's documented PayPal-Request-Id idempotency; no PayPal call is made. Assumes the documented behaviour that a repeated PayPal-Request-Id returns the original order, and that every retry falls inside PayPal's key-retention window. The PayPal sandbox run needs PayPal keys.

Current policy modelled from apps/web/src/server/payments.ts and gate-ports.ts: when every PayPal response is lost after the gate passed, the hold is kept and the order stays "confirmed"; a new purchase of the same product and variant is refused (OUTCOME_UNKNOWN) while it is unsettled; the duplicate check counts it whatever its age; reconcileUnknownOrders re-sends the original create when the buyer comes back. "Before" rows replay the same scenarios with the earlier behaviour. Definite 4xx failures, which still release the hold, are not exercised.

Reconciliation is modelled for saved-PayPal (vault) orders only, as the code does; an unknown-outcome order paid through the PayPal popup is never reconciled and keeps that item blocked. In every simulated lost response PayPal had created the order; a request that never reached PayPal was not modelled.
Timings are scripted per family with seeded random gaps. The resend-after-timeout race is placed on purpose so the resend reaches the gate just after the first attempt gives up.

Session state is modelled as read on arrival and written on completion, last writer wins; two tabs get independent state (worst case). The web app's real session store and database were not exercised; the duplicate check reads simulated orders the way gate-ports.ts reads the orders table.
Key 2 is a stub that agrees exactly when key 1 does; the real classifier needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
The random-id baseline only changes the id sent to PayPal. The gate's own duplicate guard and reservations run in both configurations.

details.label: Simulation of PayPal's documented PayPal-Request-Id idempotency; no PayPal call is made
details.requestId: paypalRequestId('order', cart.hash, readback.id), computed by runGate (orderRequestId)

configurations.unbound: PayPal-Request-Id = fresh random id per pay attempt, reused only across the HTTP client's own retries in one call
configurations.current: Lost PayPal answer: hold kept, order stays confirmed (outcome unknown); same product+variant refused (OUTCOME_UNKNOWN) until settled; unknown orders count as recent duplicates at any age; reconciliation on return re-sends the original request id
configurations.hold_kept: Lost PayPal answer: hold kept, order stays confirmed; duplicate check looks back 10 minutes only; no reconciliation
configurations.before_fix: Lost PayPal answer: hold released, order failed, buyer told nothing was charged
